column3: Ridges of wind-blown sand; the Kalahari is the largest continuous body of sand in the world.

column6: Explain that the red colour comes from iron oxide (rust) coating the sand grains.

column3: A fig tree whose roots grow into cracks in rock; an example of biotic weathering.
column4: On rocky hills and kopjes, such as the Tsodilo Hills and the hills of eastern Botswana.
column5: As the roots grow thicker they widen the cracks and slowly split the rock apart.
column6: Show guests the pale roots pressed flat against the rock and pushing into its cracks.
column7: The roots go into cracks in search of water and nutrients, and split the rock as they grow.
